findings.message: The configuration holds the key "privateKey", which names a seed, a mnemonic or a private key. The tool never reads one, and the value is not shown.
findings.fix: Remove the key from the file and from the history of the repository, and treat it as exposed: move what it controls to a new key. An oracle configuration lists public addresses only.

findings.message: Asset WETH on arbitrum is priced on Arbitrum, a rollup with a sequencer uptime feed, but the configuration declares no sequencer check. While the sequencer is down, most users cannot add collateral or repay, while some can still reach the chain through L1, and stale prices drive liquidations when it comes back.
findings.fix: Read the sequencer uptime feed of the network before every read of a price, revert while it answers 1, and declare it under sequencer.

basis.text: While the sequencer of a rollup is down, most users cannot send transactions but some can still reach the chain through L1, which can distort liquidations; the uptime feed answers 0 when the sequencer is up and 1 when it is down.
The example consumer of the guide says that a contract reading feeds on an L2 network has to read the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed as well, so that its data holds up when the sequencer is down.
basis.source: Chainlink: Using Data Feeds on EVM Chains

findings.message: Asset WBTC on arbitrum scales the answer by 18 decimals, but its feed answers with 8: every price is too low by a factor of 10,000,000,000, which lets positions be liquidated at once. The Chainlink API reference says decimals() gives the decimals of the answer.
findings.fix: Scale by the decimals of the feed, or read decimals() from the feed at run time and write scaleDecimals as "feed".

basis.text: The decimals function of AggregatorV3Interface returns how many decimals the answer carries; answers are kept as fixed-point numbers.

findings.message: The sequencer check of asset WBTC on arbitrum has no gracePeriod, so prices are used the moment the sequencer is back, before users who could not reach the chain had a chance to add collateral or repay. The Chainlink page asks for a grace period, and its example waits 3600 seconds.
findings.fix: Wait a grace period after the sequencer comes back, counted from startedAt of the uptime feed, such as the 3600 seconds of the example of the Chainlink page.

basis.text: Once the sequencer is back, an application should wait for a grace period, counted from the startedAt time of the uptime feed, before it takes answers from a data feed; the example contract of the page waits 3600 seconds.

findings.message: The price of asset USDC on base is fixed in the configuration at 1, and the asset is used as collateral: if it loses its peg, the protocol still values it at 1, lends against it at that value and does not liquidate the loans it backs. The Chainlink page on selecting feeds warns that stablecoins and wrapped assets can lose their peg. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org.
findings.fix: Price the asset from a feed, with an upper bound such as a ceiling for a stablecoin, so that a loss of the peg reaches the protocol.

basis.text: Extreme events can pull stablecoins, synthetic assets and currencies off their peg, and the hack of a bridge can split a wrapped asset from the asset under it; the page advises circuit breakers for such events.
For stablecoins the page asks protocols to weigh the risk of a price above the peg and to think about a ceiling on the value of each one, while still following a fall of the price in full.

findings.own: refusing a fixed price for collateral is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org; the Chainlink page warns that pegs break and asks for ceilings, but names no rule for a fixed price

findings.message: Asset ARB on arbitrum has no maxStaleness, so the protocol takes an answer of any age; its feed has a heartbeat of 86,400 seconds (24 hours), and an answer older than that means the feed has stopped or lags. The Chainlink overview asks an application to compare updatedAt with the heartbeat and to pause when the answer is older.
findings.fix: Give the asset a maxStaleness in seconds, from the heartbeat of the feed on its network, and list updatedAt in answerChecks.

basis.text: An application is told to compare the updatedAt time that latestRoundData returns with the heartbeat, or with a limit it sets for itself, and to pause or move to another mode when the answer is older than that.
basis.source: Chainlink: What are Chainlink Data Feeds?

basis.text: latestRoundData returns the round id, the answer, the start and update times of the round and answeredInRound, while latestAnswer gives the answer with no time to judge its freshness by.

findings.message: The address of the sequencer uptime feed of asset ARB on arbitrum is "0x5e0", which has 3 characters after 0x, not 40; an address is 0x followed by 40 hex digits. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org.
findings.fix: Write the address of the proxy as 0x and 40 hex digits, as the list of feed addresses of the network shows it.
findings.own: reading an address as 0x and 40 hex digits is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org; the pages show addresses in that form but set no rule for a configuration

findings.message: Asset WETH on arbitrum is used as collateral and has one price source and no fallback, so a feed that stops, lags or is pushed off the market moves every loan it backs at once, and the protocol has nothing to compare it with. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org.
findings.fix: Give the collateral a fallback of another kind (a second oracle or a time-weighted average price) and say what the protocol does when the two disagree, or record why one source is enough.

basis.text: Where a feed depends on one source or one provider, the page asks for bounds on the value, freshness checks, a fallback, comparison with independent references and a way to pause, above all when the feed values collateral or starts liquidations.

The page names oracle manipulation as a risk: the spot price of one decentralized exchange can be pushed with a flash loan, and the advice is a decentralized oracle network that reads many sources, or a time-weighted average price.
basis.source: ethereum.org: Smart contract security, Oracle manipulation

findings.message: Asset WETH on arbitrum accepts answers up to 172,800 seconds (48 hours) old, but the configuration gives its feed a heartbeat of 86,400 seconds (24 hours); with the margin of 10 percent the limit is 95,040 seconds. An answer older than that is one the feed should already have replaced, and liquidations and borrows go on at a price that may be gone.
findings.fix: Set maxStaleness to the heartbeat of the feed on this network plus a small margin, or record why the protocol accepts older answers.

basis.text: A new answer is written only when a round is started by the deviation threshold (the offchain value has moved far enough from the onchain one) or by the heartbeat threshold (a set time has passed since the last update), whichever comes first.
The heartbeat and the deviation threshold belong to one feed on one chain: a wrapped or liquid staking asset may have its own, and the same asset may have other values on another chain.
basis.source: Chainlink: What are Chainlink Data Feeds?

findings.message: The answer checks of asset WETH on arbitrum do not list answerPositive, so an answer of 0 or below would be used as a price; a feed that was shut down gives 0 from latestAnswer. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Chainlink pages on Data Feeds or on ethereum.org.
findings.fix: Revert on an answer of 0 or below, and list answerPositive in answerChecks.

basis.text: After a feed is shut down, latestAnswer gives 0 and a call to latestRoundData reverts.

findings.message: Asset WBTC on arbitrum accepts answers up to 3,600 seconds (1 hour) old, shorter than the heartbeat of its feed, 86,400 seconds (24 hours). In a calm market the feed is written only when the heartbeat runs out, and the round can reach the chain a little after it, so reads revert for part of every heartbeat and liquidations and repayments stop with them.
findings.fix: Set maxStaleness above the heartbeat of the feed on this network, with room for the delay before a round reaches the chain.

basis.text: A new answer is written only when a round is started by the deviation threshold (the offchain value has moved far enough from the onchain one) or by the heartbeat threshold (a set time has passed since the last update), whichever comes first.

Feeds do not stream prices: the answer changes when the price moves past the deviation threshold or when the heartbeat has run out, a heartbeat can last several hours, and the round it starts may reach the chain a little after it.
basis.source: Chainlink: What are Chainlink Data Feeds?
